Hermitian H with ||H||_op<=1 and every real t,

 Tr rho_N exp[t sum_(i=1)^N(H_i-Tr(tau_N H)I)]
          <= A exp(B N t^2).                            (H)

The constants are fixed uniformly in N; tau_N may vary with N. There is
no Young-sector assumption. Define tau=tau_N, sigma_r=tau^tensorr,

 chi_P^2(rho_r||sigma_r)=Tr rho_r^2 sigma_r^(-1)-1,
 q=r/N,
 L=e(B+2)(d^2+1)/kappa,
 y=Lq/(1-q).

For every integer 2<=r<N with y<1,

 chi_P^2(rho_r||tau^tensorr) <= A^2 y^2/(1-y).          (T1)

In particular, with the explicit constants

 c=1/(2L+1),  C=8 A^2 L^2,

one has for every integer 1<=r<=cN,

 chi_P^2(rho_r||tau^tensorr) <= C(r/N)^2,
 D(rho_r||tau^tensorr) <= log(1+chi_P^2)
                       <= C(r/N)^2,                   (T2)

where the relative entropy uses natural logarithms. At r=1 both
quantities are exactly zero. Thus (T2) applies eventually to every

The quadratic rate is attained by a fully separable family satisfying
(H); see the construction below. Concentration by itself is therefore
not an entanglement witness.

Choose a Hermitian, traceless Hilbert-Schmidt orthonormal basis

 mu_a=Tr tau F_a,  A_a=F_a-mu_a I,

# Centered local Petz entropy from uniform collective concentration

8 October 2026, thermal scientific lead. Internally reconstructed proof candidate. This freezes the proof before reading the fresh target-only derivation. The parent/integration supplied the directional generating-polynomial and real-polarization route as shared guidance. The exact normalization, constants, full proof and operational scope below were derived here. No entanglement assertion or matching upper protocol is inferred. External correctness, formal validation and historical priority are UNKNOWN.

## 1. Theorem

Fix d>=2, kappa>0, A>=1 and B>=0. Let rho_N be a permutation-invariant state on (C^d)^tensor N and let tau_N=rho_{N,1} satisfy tau_N>=kappa I. Suppose, for every Hermitian one-site H with ||H||op<=1 and every real t,

    Tr rho_N exp[t sum_{i=1}^N(H_i-Tr(tau_N H)I)]
       <= A exp(BNt^2).

Set s=d^2-1, alpha=r/N, and

    x=2e^2(B+2)s alpha/[kappa(1-alpha)^2].

For 1<=r<N and x<1,

    chi_P^2(rho_{N,r} || tau_N^tensor r)
       :=Tr[rho_{N,r}^2(tau_N^tensor r)^-1]-1
       <=A^2 x^2/(1-x),
    D(rho_{N,r} || tau_N^tensor r)<=A^2 x^2/(1-x).

In particular, for

    alpha<=min{1/2,kappa/[16e^2(B+2)s]},

one has the fully explicit uniform bound

    chi_P^2, D <=128 A^2 e^4(B+2)^2 s^2 kappa^-2 (r/N)^2.

Every r_N=o(N) eventually satisfies this range. At r=1 both quantities are exactly zero, for every N with faithful tau, independently of the numerical range. The theorem permits fixed faithful marginals far from I/d. It makes no within-sector, exact-weight, singlet, energy-diagonal or noncommuting-factorization assumption. A negative B cannot hold for a nonempty class for all t: scalar Jensen makes the centered MGF at least one, while A exp(BNt^2) would tend to zero. Thus taking B>=0 loses no legal instance.

## 2. Normalized centered one-site basis and complex Gram

Choose Hermitian traceless T_1,...,T_s with

    Tr(T_a T_b)=delta_ab.

These are Hilbert-Schmidt normalized; there is no extra factor d in the convention. Write b_a=Tr(tau_N T_a) and B_a=T_a-b_a I. Then tau_N=I/d+sum_a b_a T_a, and Tr(tau_N B_a)=0.

For inner product <U,V>_tau=Tr(tau U^dagger V), the identity has norm one and is orthogonal to all B_a. Their complex Hermitian Gram is

    G_ab=Tr(tau B_a B_b).
